title: Optimizing Microgrid Composition for Sustainable Data Centers
problem: Data centers increasingly use colocated microgrids with renewable energy and storage, but lack tools to assess how microgrid sizing and composition affect long-term sustainability and power reliability. Existing research focuses on operational vs embodied carbon tradeoffs but not on microgrid design optimization.
motivation: Energy demand for computing grows faster than grid infrastructure. Microgrids promise sustainability improvements, but design decisions (renewable capacity, storage sizing, mix) significantly impact operational and embodied emissions. Operators need systematic guidance for planning.
method: Extend Vessim (computing/energy co-simulator) with detailed renewable energy generation models from NREL's System Advisor Model (SAM). Implement multi-horizon black-box optimization to explore efficient microgrid compositions. Simulate workload-renewable-storage interaction capturing both operational and embodied emissions.
key_novelty: First integrated framework for co-optimizing data center computing workloads with renewable microgrid composition, capturing embodied carbon of infrastructure.
contributions: Integration of NREL SAM renewable generation models into Vessim
Multi-horizon black-box optimization for microgrid sizing
Joint optimization of operational and embodied emissions
Framework for informed microgrid design in data center planning

metrics.focus: Long-term sustainability, power reliability, embodied and operational emissions
metrics.evaluation: Black-box optimization convergence, microgrid configuration tradeoffs

limitations: Abstract only - no optimization results, no specific microgrid configurations evaluated, unclear scalability to large systems
primary_theme: Sustainable data center design through energy co-optimization
